title: Ezekiel Chapter 43 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 43 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 43 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 43.

questions.question: From which direction did the glory of the God of Israel come?
questions.correctAnswer: East
questions.explanation: The verse states the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east.

questions.question: Where did the glory of the LORD enter according to Ezekiel 43?
options: By the gate toward the west
By the gate toward the east
questions.correctAnswer: By the gate toward the east
questions.explanation: The glory of the LORD came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east.

questions.question: What was the effect of the glory of the LORD filling the house?
options: The house was filled with glory
questions.correctAnswer: The house was filled with glory
questions.explanation: The spirit took Ezekiel into the inner court and the glory of the LORD filled the house.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel heard God speaking to him from outside the house.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel heard God speaking to him out of the house, not outside.

questions.question: What did God say would no longer happen in the house of Israel?
options: They will no longer defile the house
They will no longer build altars
They will no longer worship idols
They will no longer fight enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They will no longer defile the house
questions.explanation: God said the house of Israel shall no more defile His holy name, neither they nor their kings by their whoredom or by the carcases of their kings.

questions.question: True or False: God was angry because the house of Israel set their thresholds and posts by His, defiling His holy name.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: God states that in setting their thresholds by His thresholds and posts by His posts, they defiled His holy name and He consumed them in anger.

questions.question: What must the house of Israel put away for God to dwell in their midst forever?
options: Their whoredom and the carcases of their kings
questions.correctAnswer: Their whoredom and the carcases of their kings
questions.explanation: God commands them to put away their whoredom and the carcases of their kings far from Him to dwell in the midst of them forever.

questions.question: True or False: The glory of the LORD was seen coming from the west in Ezekiel 43.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The glory of the LORD came from the east, not the west.

questions.question: To whom did the man speaking say 'Son of man' in Ezekiel 43?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel
questions.explanation: The man addressed Ezekiel as 'Son of man'.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 43, what did the spirit do to Ezekiel after the glory entered the house?
options: Took him to the inner court
Made him fall on his face
Sent him to the river Chebar
Commanded him to build an altar
questions.correctAnswer: Took him to the inner court
questions.explanation: The spirit took Ezekiel up and brought him into the inner court where the glory filled the house.

questions.question: What was Ezekiel instructed to show to the house of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: The pattern of the house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was instructed to show the house to the house of Israel so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities and measure the pattern.

questions.question: True or False: The earth shined with God's glory as described in Ezekiel 43.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:2 states that the earth shined with His glory.

questions.question: What was the sound of God's voice compared to in Ezekiel 43?
questions.correctAnswer: Noise of many waters
questions.explanation: God's voice was like the noise of many waters.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 43, what was the first measurement given for the altar's bottom?
questions.correctAnswer: One cubit
questions.explanation: The bottom of the altar shall be one cubit according to the measurements given.

questions.question: Which comes first according to the order of instructions in Ezekiel 43?
options: Showing the house pattern to Israel
Giving a young bullock for a sin offering
Preparing the altar for burnt offerings
questions.correctAnswer: God's glory entering the house
questions.explanation: God's glory entering the house happens first (v.4-5), before instructions about the house pattern or offerings.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 43 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 43 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is the purpose of showing the house to the house of Israel according to Ezekiel 43?
options: To make them ashamed of their iniquities
To encourage them to build a new temple
To remind them of the past glory
questions.correctAnswer: To make them ashamed of their iniquities
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:10 states that the house is shown to the house of Israel so they may be ashamed of their iniquities. This purpose is reinforced by verse 11, which instructs to show them the form and laws of the house so they may keep and do them.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 43, what should the house of Israel do after seeing the form and laws of the house?
options: Keep the whole form and all the ordinances and do them
Build an altar on the mountain
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the whole form and all the ordinances and do them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:11 commands that after seeing the form and laws of the house, the house of Israel should keep the whole form and all the ordinances and do them, emphasizing obedience and faithfulness.

questions.question: Where is the whole limit of the house to be most holy according to Ezekiel 43?
options: Upon the top of the mountain round about
In the valley beside the river
At the entrance to the city
questions.correctAnswer: Upon the top of the mountain round about
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:12 clearly states that the whole limit of the house shall be most holy upon the top of the mountain round about, indicating the sacredness of the temple's location.

questions.question: What is the measurement of one cubit as described in Ezekiel 43 for the altar?
options: A cubit and a hand breadth
A span and a finger breadth
questions.correctAnswer: A cubit and a hand breadth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:13 defines the cubit used for measuring the altar as a cubit and a hand breadth, giving a specific standard for the altar's construction.

questions.question: How high is the altar from the bottom upon the ground to the lower settle according to Ezekiel 43?
questions.correctAnswer: Two cubits
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:14 specifies that from the bottom upon the ground to the lower settle is two cubits, indicating the altar's structure details.

questions.question: What special feature does the altar have from the altar upward according to Ezekiel 43?
questions.correctAnswer: Four horns
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:15 states that the altar shall have four horns from the altar upward, which is a significant part of the altar's design.

questions.question: What are the dimensions of the altar's base according to Ezekiel 43?
options: Twelve cubits long and twelve cubits broad, square in four squares
Ten cubits long and ten cubits broad
Four cubits long and four cubits broad
Fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits broad
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve cubits long and twelve cubits broad, square in four squares
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:16 describes the altar as twelve cubits long and twelve cubits broad, square in the four squares thereof, indicating its size and shape.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 43, how long and broad is the settle of the altar and where do its stairs look?
options: Fourteen cubits long and broad; stairs look toward the east
Twelve cubits long and broad; stairs look toward the west
Ten cubits long and broad; stairs look toward the north
Six cubits long and broad; stairs look toward the south
questions.correctAnswer: Fourteen cubits long and broad; stairs look toward the east
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:17 states that the settle is fourteen cubits long and broad, with stairs looking toward the east, highlighting the altar's detailed construction and orientation.

questions.question: What purpose does the altar serve on the day it is made according to Ezekiel 43?
options: To offer burnt offerings and sprinkle blood
To hold the Ark of the Covenant
To be a place for sacrifices only on the Sabbath
To serve as a gathering place for the elders
questions.correctAnswer: To offer burnt offerings and sprinkle blood
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:18 explains that the ordinances of the altar on the day it is made are to offer burnt offerings and to sprinkle blood thereon, defining its ritual use.

questions.question: Who are the priests mentioned in Ezekiel 43 that are to minister to God and receive a young bullock for a sin offering?
options: The Levites of the seed of Zadok
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites of the seed of Zadok
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:19 specifies that the priests who approach to minister unto God and receive the young bullock for a sin offering are the Levites of the seed of Zadok, emphasizing their special status.

questions.question: How is the altar to be cleansed with the blood of the sin offering according to Ezekiel 43?
options: Put blood on the four horns, the four corners of the settle, and the border round about
Pour blood at the base of the altar only
Sprinkle blood on the outer wall
Burn the blood outside the sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: Put blood on the four horns, the four corners of the settle, and the border round about
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:20 instructs to put the blood on the four horns of the altar, the four corners of the settle, and the border round about to cleanse and purge it, describing the ritual purification.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 43, where is the bullock of the sin offering to be burned?
options: In the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: In the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:21 specifies that the bullock of the sin offering shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary, showing careful separation of the purification rites.

questions.question: What is the significance of the seven days of offerings and purging in Ezekiel 43?
options: To prepare, purge, and consecrate the altar
To atone for the sins of the people
questions.correctAnswer: To prepare, purge, and consecrate the altar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:25-26 explain that seven days are set to prepare every day a sin offering and other offerings, purging and purifying the altar and consecrating the priests, emphasizing holiness and readiness.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 43:27 promise will happen if the priests follow the instructions to purge and consecrate the altar?
options: The LORD will accept their burnt and peace offerings
They will receive blessings of wealth
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will accept their burnt and peace offerings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:27 promises that once the altar is purified and consecrated, the priests shall make burnt and peace offerings upon it, and the LORD will accept them, highlighting obedience and divine acceptance.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 43 teaches that the altar must be cleansed with a kid of the goats on the second day, as well as with a bullock on the first day.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:21-22 describes that the bullock is offered on the first day for sin offering, and on the second day a kid of the goats without blemish is offered to cleanse the altar, confirming the process over two days.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 43 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 43.

questions.question: Who are the priests mentioned in Ezekiel 43:19 that are to receive the young bullock for a sin offering?
options: Priests from the tribe of Levi
Levites of the seed of Zadok
questions.correctAnswer: Levites of the seed of Zadok
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:19 specifically instructs the offering to be given to the priests who are Levites of the seed of Zadok, those who approach to minister to God.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 43:20, where is the blood of the sin offering to be applied?
options: On the four horns, four corners of the settle, and the border around
questions.correctAnswer: On the four horns, four corners of the settle, and the border around
questions.explanation: The verse details putting blood on the four horns of the altar, the four corners of the settle, and the border round about to cleanse and purge the altar.

questions.question: Where must the bullock of the sin offering be burned according to Ezekiel 43:21?
options: In the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: In the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:21 commands that the bullock is to be burned in the appointed place of the house but outside the sanctuary itself.

questions.question: What is offered on the second day as a sin offering in Ezekiel 43:22?
options: A kid of the goats without blemish
questions.correctAnswer: A kid of the goats without blemish
questions.explanation: The verse says a kid of the goats without blemish is offered on the second day for a sin offering.

questions.question: What two animals are offered after the cleansing is completed according to Ezekiel 43:23?
options: A young bullock and a ram out of the flock
questions.correctAnswer: A young bullock and a ram out of the flock
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:23 instructs that after cleansing, a young bullock without blemish and a ram without blemish from the flock should be offered.

questions.question: What substance are the priests to cast upon the burnt offerings as described in Ezekiel 43:24?
questions.correctAnswer: Salt
questions.explanation: The priests are commanded to cast salt upon the burnt offerings before offering them up to the LORD, as per Ezekiel 43:24.

questions.question: How many days are designated for preparing daily sin offerings and other sacrifices during the altar's purification in Ezekiel 43:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:25 states that seven days are set for preparing a goat for sin offering daily along with a young bullock and a ram without blemish.

questions.question: What must the priests do during the seven days of purging the altar according to Ezekiel 43:26?
questions.correctAnswer: Consecrate themselves
questions.explanation: The priests shall purge and purify the altar and consecrate themselves during the seven days as described in Ezekiel 43:26.

questions.question: What happens after the seven days of preparation and purging as stated in Ezekiel 43:27?
options: Burnt offerings and peace offerings begin
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt offerings and peace offerings begin
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:27 explains that on the eighth day and thereafter, priests shall make burnt offerings and peace offerings upon the altar, and God will accept them.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is closely connected to the altar ordinances in Ezekiel 43 and also contains detailed altar instructions?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 27
questions.explanation: Exodus 27 provides detailed instructions on altar construction and offerings, which closely parallels the altar ordinances in Ezekiel 43:13-27.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's glory filling the temple as seen in Ezekiel 43:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 21
questions.explanation: Revelation 21 describes the glory of God filling the New Jerusalem, echoing the vision of God's glory filling the temple in Ezekiel 43:5.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'purge' or 'cleanse' in Ezekiel 43:20 is likely related to which concept in the Old Testament sacrificial system?
questions.correctAnswer: Tahara (purification)
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root behind 'cleanse' or 'purge' in Ezekiel 43:20 relates to tahara, meaning purification, a key concept in Old Testament sacrificial rites.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 43:11 where the vision of the house is described with repeated phrases and detailed forms?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:11 uses parallelism by repeating phrases like 'all the forms thereof' and 'all the ordinances thereof' to emphasize the completeness of the vision.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 43:7 promises that God will dwell forever in the midst of the children of Israel, and their kings will no longer defile His holy name by whoredom or carcasses in high places.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:7 clearly states God's promise to dwell among Israel forever and that neither they nor their kings will defile His holy name as before.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 43:8 states that the people defiled God’s holy name only by disobedience in speech, not by any physical actions related to thresholds or walls.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:8 explains that the defilement was through physical acts involving thresholds, posts, and a wall between God and them, not merely disobedience in speech.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 43 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 43 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 43:7 reveal about the holiness of God in relation to Israel's past sins?
options: God will dwell with Israel forever and no longer allow defilement by their sins.
God will continually punish Israel for their past sins.
God will forget Israel's sins but not dwell among them.
God will only dwell with Israel as long as they perform sacrifices.
questions.correctAnswer: God will dwell with Israel forever and no longer allow defilement by their sins.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:7 states that God's throne and feet will be in the midst of Israel forever and that He will no longer allow their holy name to be defiled by their whoredom or the carcasses of their kings, indicating a permanent restoration of holiness.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 43:12, what is the significance of the 'top of the mountain' concerning the law of the house?
options: It marks the boundary of the most holy place surrounding the house.
It is where the altar must be built.
It is the location where sacrifices must be offered.
It is the place where the priests shall dwell.
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the boundary of the most holy place surrounding the house.
questions.explanation: Verse 12 declares that upon the top of the mountain, the whole limit around the house shall be most holy, showing the sanctity of the temple area and God's presence.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is taught by the detailed altar measurements in Ezekiel 43:13-17?
options: The doctrine of God's order and holiness in worship.
The doctrine of justification by faith alone.
The doctrine of predestination and election.
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's order and holiness in worship.
questions.explanation: The precise measurements and design of the altar emphasize God's demand for order, reverence, and holiness in worship (Ezekiel 43:13-17). This reflects the sacred nature of approaching God.

questions.question: How does the glory of God entering through the east gate in Ezekiel 43:4-5 symbolize a broader redemptive theme?
options: It symbolizes God's renewed presence and restoration among His people.
It represents the exile of Israel to the east.
It indicates the destruction of the temple.
It symbolizes the judgment coming from the west.
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's renewed presence and restoration among His people.
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 describe the glory of the LORD entering the house by the east gate and filling the house, symbolizing God's return and restored fellowship with Israel, a key redemptive theme of God's covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 43:9 teach about the conditions for God's presence dwelling with Israel forever?
options: Israel must put away their idolatry and the remains of their kings' sins.
Israel must build a larger temple.
questions.correctAnswer: Israel must put away their idolatry and the remains of their kings' sins.
questions.explanation: Verse 9 commands Israel to remove their whoredom and the carcasses of their kings far from God so that He may dwell in their midst forever, linking holiness with God's abiding presence.

questions.question: What attribute of God is primarily revealed in Ezekiel 43:2, where His voice is described as 'like a noise of many waters' and the earth shines with His glory?
questions.correctAnswer: God's majesty and overwhelming power.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:2 depicts the glory of God coming from the east with a voice like many waters and the earth shining, illustrating God's majestic and powerful nature.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 43:19-20 describe the purification process of the altar, and what doctrinal truth does this illustrate?
options: The altar is cleansed by the blood of a sin offering, illustrating the doctrine of atonement.
The altar is cleansed by water, illustrating purification by ritual washing.
The altar is cleansed by fire alone, illustrating God's judgment.
The altar is cleansed by incense, illustrating prayer.
questions.correctAnswer: The altar is cleansed by the blood of a sin offering, illustrating the doctrine of atonement.
questions.explanation: Verses 19-20 outline using the blood of a young bullock for sin offering to cleanse the altar, showing the principle of atonement through sacrificial blood covering sin.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that detailed temple visions like Ezekiel 43 are merely mythological and lack theological significance. What does Ezekiel 43:10-11 actually teach about the purpose of these visions?
options: They serve as a pattern to show Israel their iniquities and instruct them in obedience.
They are symbolic stories with no practical application.
They are predictions of political events only.
They are meant to be ignored by Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: They serve as a pattern to show Israel their iniquities and instruct them in obedience.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:10-11 explains that the visions reveal the house's form and ordinances so Israel may be ashamed of their sins and keep God's laws, showing theological and moral purpose rather than myth.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 43:23-24, what is the significance of salt being cast upon the burnt offerings, and which doctrine does this highlight?
options: Salt symbolizes covenant purity, highlighting the doctrine of covenant faithfulness.
Salt is for preservation, highlighting eternal life.
Salt is a seasoning, highlighting celebratory worship.
Salt represents judgment, highlighting God's wrath.
questions.correctAnswer: Salt symbolizes covenant purity, highlighting the doctrine of covenant faithfulness.
questions.explanation: Verse 24 mentions priests casting salt on offerings, symbolizing the enduring, pure covenant between God and His people, emphasizing faithfulness in worship.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 43:26-27 teach about the process of sanctification for the priests and the altar?
options: Seven days of purging and consecration lead to ongoing acceptable worship.
Sanctification is only for the altar, not the priests.
Sanctification is achieved through offerings only.
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days of purging and consecration lead to ongoing acceptable worship.
questions.explanation: Verses 26-27 describe a seven-day consecration period for purging the altar and priests, indicating a process of sanctification necessary for worship to be accepted.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's holiness and Israel's restoration is conveyed by Ezekiel 43:8 and Ezekiel 43:9?
options: Israel's past defilement caused God's anger, but repentance allows His dwelling among them forever.
God will never forgive Israel's defilement.
Israel can ignore God's holiness and still be restored.
God's anger is permanent and cannot be removed.
questions.correctAnswer: Israel's past defilement caused God's anger, but repentance allows His dwelling among them forever.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:8 states Israel defiled God's name causing His anger, while 43:9 calls for putting away sins so God may dwell forever, teaching holiness requires repentance for restoration.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 43:3 reveal about the continuity of Ezekiel's visions and their theological significance?
options: The vision of God's glory is consistent with earlier visions, confirming divine revelation.
The vision contradicts previous ones and is confusing.
The vision is unrelated to the destruction of the city.
The vision is purely symbolic with no real meaning.
questions.correctAnswer: The vision of God's glory is consistent with earlier visions, confirming divine revelation.
questions.explanation: Verse 3 notes the vision matches earlier ones by the river Chebar and at the city's destruction, indicating theological continuity of God's presence and judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Ezekiel 43:6 where the man speaks to Ezekiel from the house while standing beside him?
questions.correctAnswer: God's communicative presence and guidance.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:6 shows God speaking from the house and a man standing by Ezekiel, emphasizing God's attribute of revealing Himself and guiding His prophet.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 43:16 teach about the altar and its symbolism in the worship of Israel?
options: The altar is perfectly square, symbolizing completeness and perfection in worship.
The altar is triangular, symbolizing the Trinity.
The altar is circular, symbolizing eternity.
The altar is irregular, symbolizing human imperfection.
questions.correctAnswer: The altar is perfectly square, symbolizing completeness and perfection in worship.
questions.explanation: Verse 16 describes the altar as twelve cubits long and broad, square in four squares, symbolizing God's perfection and completeness in worship.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is gained by synthesizing Ezekiel 43:11 and Ezekiel 43:27 regarding obedience and worship?
options: Obedience to God's laws leads to accepted worship and fellowship with God.
Obedience is only about external ritual, not heart transformation.
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's laws leads to accepted worship and fellowship with God.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 43:11 commands Israel to keep the form and ordinances, while 43:27 promises acceptable offerings after consecration, teaching that obedience and sanctification are essential for true worship.
